messages:
Maya: Heads up — after the Cilium 1.18 rollout to west-2 gpu-pools we started seeing pod-to-pod packet loss and intermittent RDMA hangs :grimacing:
Maya: Symptoms: 20-40% ping loss between GPU pods on the same nodepair, some NCCL jobs stalled, conntrack counts skyrocketed on affected nodes.
Oliver: Which node image + kernel? MTU changes?
Maya: Kernel 5.15.0-101, node image rdx-gpu-ubuntu-2204-2026-02. No MTU changes in the kubelet config. We did flip to Cilium 1.18.0-rc2 yesterday.
Priya: Do you have `conntrack -S` or `ss` output? Could be conntrack timeouts/alloc leak after bpf change.
Maya: Paste from one of the bad nodes:```
Conntrack entries: 429496
conntrack: tcp timewait: 7200
ss -s: Total: 32768 (estab 1024, closed 21476, orphaned 0, timewait 21476)
iping stats: 100 packets transmitted, 62 received, 38% packet loss, rtt min/avg/max = 0.2/1.4/12 ms
```
Ben: 38% is huge. Any drops in dmesg or OOM?
Maya: dmesg shows repeated "cilium-agent: conntrack: could not allocate" errors and a lot of BPF verifier warnings during agent start.
Oliver: That smells like the new BPF program pushes state into conntrack and we're hitting conntrack table limits. What are the conntrack_max and hashsize?
Maya: `sysctl net.netfilter.nf_conntrack_max` -> 262144 on affected nodes. `cat /proc/sys/net/netfilter/nf_conntrack_count` -> 245800 (close to limit).
Priya: Are we using host-reachable services / NodePort/host-gw mode anywhere in those pools? That could increase entries.
Maya: Mostly ipip + host-gw fallback for some older clusters. This pool is using tunnel mode with `enable-bpf-masquerade=true` per the 1.18 defaults.
Ben: Could also be conntrack timeouts being longer so entries pile up — if new agent doesn't prune established flows correctly. Any telemetry from Cilium about CT hit rates?
Maya: Cilium metrics show conntrack_entries_total spike right after the rollout window (~11:05 UTC).
Oliver: Immediate mitigation: scale down Cilium to 1.17 config or roll back the deployment in west-2 canary. Also bump nf_conntrack_max to 1M temporarily on affected nodes.
Priya: Agree. We should also set `bpf.conntrack.max_entries` if available in the chart and increase table size so bpf doesn't drop.
Maya: Doing a quick node sysctl update on the three hottest nodes now: `sysctl -w net.netfilter.nf_conntrack_max=1000000` (running as root) — will monitor.
deploy-bot: rollback job triggered by @Maya: `helm rollback cilium 3 --namespace kube-system` (canary) — started at 11:28 UTC.
Maya: After bumping conntrack, packet loss dropped to ~4% on the tested node within 90s. Still seeing some lingering flows but jobs resumed.
Oliver: Good. Next: revert the full pool or pin to 1.17 until we can reproduce in staging. Also open an issue with Cilium linking BPF verifier logs and conntrack counts.
Ben: I'll reproduce locally with same kernel + MTU + RDMA workload to see if RDMA path triggers extra CT entries.
Priya: Add test: run iperf RDMA + lots of short TCP connections, measure conntrack growth. Include `bpf logs` from agent.
Maya: I'll keep canary rolled back and let SRE watch for any regression. We'll prepare a postmortem note with timeline, metrics graphs, and the failing node dmesg excerpts.
Oliver: TY all. Priorities: (1) keep rollback in west-2, (2) collect full CT dumps + BPF verifier output, (3) coordinate with Cilium 1.18 maintainers for root cause.
Maya: Filed internal ticket INFRA-3251 with attached logs.
Ben: ping me when you have the BPF verifier output. I'll start a small reproduce run tonight. :coffee:
Priya: Leaving note — if anyone sees new pods flapping in the next hour, escalate to pagers.
Maya: Will do. Thanks everyone :thumbsup:
